newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Ocensa gets $307 mln syndicated loan.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Ocensa gets $307 mln syndicated loan.

text.p: Oleoducto Central SA (Ocensa) said it signed a 3-1/2 year $307 million syndicated loan in New York Friday to help finance the construction of a pipeline linking the Cusiana oil fields in Colombia's eastern plains to the Caribbean port of Covenas.

The loan was co-lead managed by Chase Manhattan Bank and the Industrial Bank of Japan, Ocensa said in a statement. It said the loan would be used to pay off a bridge loan that carried a higher interest rate. It did not specify the interest rate on the new credit line.

Construction of the 500-mile (800 km) Cusiana-Coveas pipeline, which began in November of last year, is expected to be completed by late next year at a total cost of about $2 billion. The pipeline, from the huge Cusiana field operated by British Petroleum Co Plc, will have a capacity to carry up to 556,000 barrels of crude oil per day.
Colombia's state oil company, Ecopetrol, is a leading partner in Ocensa along with BP, Total Pipeline Colombia SA, Triton Pipeline Colombia Inc and TCPL International.
